title: Institutional progress is widening on paper while justice, information access, and inclusive voice remain uneven
source_unit: United Nations Statistics Division, Sustainable Development Goals Report 2026, Goal 16: Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions
geography: Global country and institutional reporting across SDG 16 indicators

homicide_change.unit: percent change in global homicide rate

2030_gap.value: current trajectory remains short of the SDG ambition to significantly reduce violence

distribution.value: violence remains concentrated in a few regions and disproportionately burdens women and children

observations.method: UNSD compilation of SDG 16 country indicators and global estimates.
observations.uncertainty: Global aggregates mask conflict, reporting, definition, and regional coverage differences; a trend in homicide does not summarize all forms of violence or insecurity.
observations.subgroup: Women, children, civilians in conflict-affected settings, and populations in regions with concentrated violence.
observations.counterinterpretation: The decline in the global homicide rate is meaningful progress even though it is uneven and insufficient for the stated target.

observations.period: 2015-2026; legal access to information and justice implementation

denominator.unit: countries covered by SDG 16 institutional reporting

information_laws.unit: countries with adopted access-to-information laws as of 2026

implementation_gap.value: compliance with access-to-information frameworks remains inconsistent

bribery_gradient.unit: times higher bribery rate in low-income than high-income countries

observations.method: UNSD synthesis of SDG legal-framework, public-integrity, and governance indicators.
observations.uncertainty: Legal adoption is not equivalent to timely access, enforcement, service quality, or freedom from informal barriers; cross-country bribery measures vary in coverage and reporting.
observations.subgroup: Information seekers, public-service users, low-income populations, journalists, civil society, and people interacting with public officials.
observations.counterinterpretation: Expansion of legal frameworks can create durable institutional capacity even when enforcement and everyday usability lag.

denominator.unit: countries assessed under Paris Principles accreditation reporting

fully_compliant.unit: countries with fully compliant national human-rights institutions in 2025

baseline.unit: countries with fully compliant institutions in 2015

plateau.value: the number of compliant institutions plateaued in 2025

observations.method: UNSD reporting drawing on national human-rights institution compliance with the Paris Principles.
observations.uncertainty: Accreditation status measures institutional standards and independence on a formal framework; it does not directly measure the effectiveness of remedies or public trust.
observations.subgroup: People seeking rights protection, civil-society organizations, national oversight bodies, and populations in states with partially compliant or absent institutions.
observations.counterinterpretation: The increase from 70 to 89 fully compliant institutions shows institutional diffusion despite a recent slowdown.

denominator.unit: global political and public-service representation reporting frame

women_speaker_appointments.unit: percent of new speaker appointments held by women

decision_power.value: women and young people remain underrepresented in parliaments, public service, and the judiciary and are often excluded from the most influential roles

institutional_link.value: underrepresentation limits whose experiences shape decisions under conflict, climate, economic, and technological disruption

observations.method: UNSD synthesis of SDG 16 political representation and institutional inclusion indicators.
observations.uncertainty: Representation counts do not fully capture agenda-setting power, intersectional exclusion, informal influence, or policy responsiveness.
observations.subgroup: Women, young people, marginalized groups, public-service applicants, elected representatives, and communities affected by institutional decisions.
observations.counterinterpretation: Descriptive representation can improve visibility and institutional legitimacy, but it is not by itself evidence of equal policy outcomes.

related_sources.claim: UN DESA Goal 16 page and 2026 extended-report context for peace, justice, access to information, and strong institutions.
UNDP launch statement for the Fourth Global Report on SDG 16 and its slow, uneven, fragile progress framing.

boundary: This record adds an aggregate institutional-performance route linking violence, justice, public information, human-rights oversight, and inclusive political voice. It is not a respondent survey, individual justice-experience panel, country causal estimate, or respondent-level microdata analysis.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: The official UNSD 2026 Goal 16 page and linked UN/UNDP context were reviewed; violence, information access, bribery, human-rights institutions, and representation claims were cross-checked.
